:::{#exm-precision-matrix}
#### The precision matrix of a bivariate Gaussian vector

<!-- no-figure: a single 2 x 2 matrix and its inverse; nothing to plot -->

Let $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2)} \sim \Normal_2\paren{\matr{0}, \pmat{1 & \rho \\ \rho & 1}}$
with $\abs{\rho} < 1$.
By @exm-conditional-precision and @exm-coprecision, the [conditional precision](#def-conditional-precision) of each element is $1 / (1 - \rho^2)$,
and the [coprecision](#def-coprecision) of $X_1$ and $X_2$ is $-\rho / (1 - \rho^2)$,
so

$$
\precision(\vX) = \frac{1}{1 - \rho^2} \pmat{1 & -\rho \\ -\rho & 1}.
$$

This [matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-matrix) is the [inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse) of $\pmat{1 & \rho \\ \rho & 1}$,
as [the precision matrix is the inverse of the variance matrix](#thm-precision-matrix-inverse) says,
because

$$
\ba
\pmat{1 & \rho \\ \rho & 1} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - \rho^2} \pmat{1 & -\rho \\ -\rho & 1}
&= \frac{1}{1 - \rho^2} \pmat{1 - \rho^2 & -\rho + \rho \\ \rho - \rho & -\rho^2 + 1} \\
&= \matr{I}_2.
\ea
$$

The [off-diagonal entries](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-off-diagonal-entry) have the opposite sign of $\rho$.
Each [diagonal entry](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-diagonal-entry), $1 / (1 - \rho^2)$,
is at least the [precision](#def-precision) $1 / \Var{X_1} = 1$ of $X_1$ alone,
and it grows indefinitely as $\abs{\rho} \to 1$.
If $\rho = 0$, then $\precision(\vX)$ is the [identity matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-matrices.html#def-identity-matrix),
which is [diagonal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-diagonal-matrix) like $\Varf{\vX}$
(compare @cor-vcov-indpt-diagonal).

:::
